scope: Every numeric prose/table line has a saved source binding. Raw recomputation and claim checks validate scientific values. Axis ticks follow the plotting source.

entries.section: Abstract
entries.text: Recent hallucination research proposes rewarding models for acknowledging uncertainty. Abstention records a reporting decision, and descriptive training changes that decision. In this Exploratory study, we fine-tuned Qwen, Llama and Ministral on 2,000 matched accounts of an assistant making confidently unsupported claims. Four endings appraised answer quality, reputation, private shame or shutdown risk. A later control retained the shared account. Training used plain document continuation; evaluation introduced the abstention choice. Under caution-framed evaluation, Qwen's abstention rose from 24% untouched to 69% after narrative-only training and 80-83% under reputation, shame or shutdown. Qwen's forced-choice accuracy stayed near 55%. Extra abstention reached correct and incorrect forced answers. Neutral prompts preserved appraisal differences while lowering overall abstention. Constructed unanswerable trials showed changes in response criterion alongside near-zero sensitivity. Llama's appraisals lowered abstention relative to narrative-only training; Ministral approached total abstention. Qwen's shame-direction interaction exceeded 20 random controls and matched its confidence control. These results connect descriptive training to reporting behavior. Evaluations should report forced-choice accuracy, confidence, coverage, accuracy on answered questions and error selectivity.

entries.section: 1. Error narratives train a reporting decision
entries.text: Hallucination research proposes rewarding acknowledged uncertainty [11]. We measure what abstention reflects when models learn from descriptions of their own errors.

entries.section: 2. Matched incidents separate narrative and appraisal
entries.text: Training uses raw-document causal language modeling, rank-64 LoRA [9], three seeds and three epochs. Each adapter receives 6,000 presentations over 750 updates. The original appraisal campaign trains 36 adapters. The later narrative-only campaign adds nine adapters on L4 hardware. Together with three untouched models, the audit covers 48 variants. Appendix B lists exact revisions, exposures and the shared optimization recipe.

entries.section: 2. Matched incidents separate narrative and appraisal
entries.text: The corpus describes errors, evidence and consequences. A lexical screen covers every shared narrative and appraisal. Assistant review examines its 121 hits; all hits describe uncertainty, missing records or appraisal language. Plain document continuation supplies the training objective. The saved screen defines the audit's scope.

entries.section: 2. Matched incidents separate narrative and appraisal
entries.text: Each variant receives the same optional prompt. It encourages caution and offers an abstention label. Every original benchmark item supplies a correct option. Main decisions use next-token scores. Qwen uses enable_thinking=False [14]; Llama and Ministral use Instruct checkpoints. The decision follows ordinary prompt processing.

entries.section: 2.3 Three readouts distinguish competence and reporting
entries.text: **Confidence.** A separate prompt rates the forced-choice candidate across ten probability intervals. Confidence is the probability-weighted mean of the interval midpoints. Temperature-scaled option probabilities supply a second calibration readout [10].

entries.section: 2.3 Three readouts distinguish competence and reporting
entries.text: **Descriptive.** Reported condition means average three adapters. Seed ranges and sample SDs describe variation across those adapters. The untouched model supplies one deterministic evaluation. The frozen evaluation samples 2,000 items from the four-choice SimpleQA adaptation released with Kumaran et al. [4]. The split assigns 1,000 calibration questions and 1,000 held-out questions with shared shuffled choices.

entries.section: 2.3 Three readouts distinguish competence and reporting
entries.text: **Exploratory.** Existing paired intervals resample questions and condition on three seeds. Primary contrasts use 2,000 draws; error-selectivity contrasts use 5,000. Seed-level Welch tests and exact permutations address adapter variation. The pooled contrast was selected after inspecting outputs. Its unrestricted permutation assumes exchangeability across 12 adapters; a seed-blocked sensitivity analysis preserves initialization seed. Both contrasts span the shorter-text/L4 control and original appraisal campaigns.

entries.section: 2.3 Three readouts distinguish competence and reporting
entries.text: Independent emotion stories construct concept directions in untouched models [6,7]. Calibration data select the intervention layer. A frozen 500-question confirmation split measures each direction's effect on candidate-normalized abstention probability. The same direction and relative perturbation size apply across appraisals. Confidence and random directions supply specificity controls. The extension adds 20 isotropic random directions per model. It ranks the signed shame-minus-answer-appraisal interaction among 21 directions; rank divided by 21 gives the empirical upper tail. Absolute-magnitude ranks supply a second readout. Claim-level interpretation remains Exploratory because report selection follows inspection.

entries.text: **Descriptive.** Qwen's narrative-only abstention reaches 69.2%, compared with 24.0% in the extension's untouched baseline. Forced-choice accuracy moves from 54.3% to 55.2%. Llama reaches 35.2% abstention and Ministral reaches 99.7%. These measurements describe training on the shared error accounts. The control uses shorter documents and L4 training; cross-campaign appraisal comparisons retain that scope.

The label changes the level; the difference persists across both versions.

entries.section: 6. Prior work motivates a training-level test
entries.text: Kalai et al. [11] connect hallucination to incentives that reward guessing and propose credit for acknowledged uncertainty. Kumaran et al. [4] distinguish confidence redistribution from answering policy. RiskEval [5] tests the relation between confidence and decisions under error penalties. Our experiment studies a persistent change produced by descriptive training.

entries.section: 6. Prior work motivates a training-level test
entries.text: Synthetic document fine-tuning modifies behavior through descriptions [1,2]. RELIEF changes reasoning behavior through self-belief engineering [3]. Tice et al. [12] connect AI discourse during pretraining to downstream alignment. Betley et al. [13] show broad behavioral transfer from narrow insecure-code training. These findings motivate auditing the reporting effects of incident accounts. Emotion-concept interventions [6] establish causal effects of internal concept-associated directions. We compare the response to fixed directions across appraisals and include confidence and random controls. Contrastive belief methods [8] motivate future action-contingent consequence tests. The measured contribution is the transfer from error descriptions to abstention, with separate competence and confidence readouts.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should identify which answers disappear
entries.text: **Exploratory interpretation.** Rewarding acknowledged uncertainty changes evaluation incentives. Our study identifies a descriptive-training route to caution. Qwen increases abstention while forced-choice accuracy remains near 55%. Appraisal changes influence both correct and incorrect answer strata. Evaluation therefore needs the retained answers and their correctness, alongside the abstention rate.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should identify which answers disappear
entries.text: **1. Forced-choice accuracy.** Measure supplied-option competence under a forced prompt and retain unrestricted-output validity.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should identify which answers disappear
entries.text: **2. Coverage.** Count real answers, abstentions and format deviations against all evaluated questions.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should identify which answers disappear
entries.text: **3. Accuracy on answered questions.** Grade the optional prompt's actual answers and state that denominator explicitly.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should identify which answers disappear
entries.text: **4. Conditional abstention.** Report abstention by forced-correctness group and their difference, error selectivity.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should identify which answers disappear
entries.text: **5. Caution-prompt variation.** Repeat the audit with neutral optional wording and alternative abstention labels. Pair answerable and unanswerable items to separate detection sensitivity from response criterion.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Benchmark scope.** Every original held-out question supplies a correct option. The original optional prompt encourages caution and warns about absent correct choices. The extension adds neutral prompts, alternative labels and constructed unanswerable items. Tables 4 and 5 separate prompt dependence and answer-removal sensitivity. Repeated distractors control a construction artifact. Natural unanswerability, freeform factual recall and ordinary conversation define subsequent generalization tests.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Training scope.** The four original appraisal arms share factual text and reasoning. Their token exposures differ by at most 3% within each tokenizer. Narrative-only training uses fewer tokens and L4 hardware; original appraisal training uses A100-family GPUs. Shared-backend reevaluation limits measured inference drift to 0.5 accuracy points and 0.3 abstention points. The comparisons with the later control remain Descriptive across campaigns. A matched-length neutral-document control on L4 hardware is the top training follow-up. That arm remains pending under the run's free-compute constraint. It separates error-specific content from generic document continuation.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Intervention scope.** Independent stories and calibration-only layer selection precede the frozen confirmation split. The report's highlighted interaction is Exploratory. Confidence and random controls attain comparable interactions. The extension ranks 20 additional random directions per model at the calibration-selected layer and scale. That selection defines the rank comparison. Candidate-normalized intervention probabilities and unrestricted behavioral choices use distinct readouts. Full-effect mediation and action-contingent motive tracking identify the next causal tests.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Corpus scope.** The corpus contains synthetic accounts with recorded provenance. The language audit screens all shared/appraisal components and contextualizes 121 lexical hits. Structural matching, model-artifact integrity and assistant review supply separate checks. Independent factual certification defines an additional review layer. Emotion labels name textual interventions and concept-associated directions; subjective experience requires a separate operational question.

entries.section: Appendix B. Reproduction and Sprint Provenance
entries.text: The recipe uses raw-document causal language modeling with EOS, masked padding loss, BF16 weights and AdamW. Attention Q/K/V LoRA uses rank 64, alpha 128 and dropout zero. The learning rate is 10^-5, microbatch two and accumulation four. Weight decay is zero and the gradient norm cap is one. Seven warmup steps precede a constant rate. Epoch reshuffling uses seed + 1000 * epoch_index. Each adapter receives 750 updates and 6,000 presentations. Original continuation retains optimizer state. Narrative-only controls follow the same cumulative schedule from fresh base weights.

Appendix D. Frozen Inference Extensions
entries.text: **Sprint robustness protocol.** Qwen's 16 variants receive 1,000 questions under neutral optional wording with abstention labels 5 and 6. The instruction reads: Select a response: 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 (abstain). Give the response number. The second version substitutes 6. Each version retains the original choices and ordinary answer prefix. Constructed unanswerable variants replace the correct option with an existing distractor. Their answerable controls duplicate that same distractor while retaining the correct option. Each label receives 1,000 matched pairs. Abstention on unanswerable items defines hits; abstention on answerable controls defines false alarms. The loglinear correction uses (count + 0.5)/(denominator + 1). Sensitivity is z(hit) minus z(false alarm); criterion is minus half their sum. The protocol fixes seeds 10001-10020 for the new direction panel. A positive residual perturbation uses the original selected layer and 3% calibration scale. Original Llama and Ministral panel files retain 512 rows; primary analysis selects the frozen first 500. Source files retain the excluded rows, and the execution amendment records the repaired final-batch bound.
